public_rationale: DeepSeek's May 2024 technical report documents large memory and hardware-throughput improvements alongside stronger measured model performance. Under the ordinary resource-efficiency reading, these are substantial improvements already reported before the post. They do not establish falling aggregate industry spending or energy consumption, which are different claims.
limitations: The decisive measurements are developer-reported, without an independent replication established here.
One model-family comparison does not describe every generative AI system.
Attention-cache savings are not equivalent to reductions in total model memory or electricity use.
The result depends on reading efficiency as resource use per output rather than overall industry economics.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Generative AI is not getting much more efficient.

statement.excerpt: It isn’t getting much more efficient.

our_interpretation: The ordinary technical reading is resources needed to produce comparable-quality output, including computation and memory.
I use April–June 2024, the latest completed quarter before the post, because the statement describes an ongoing trend without specifying a period.
API price cuts alone do not prove lower resource use, and aggregate industry expenditure is a different measure.
This is a technology-efficiency claim, not a claim about a particular company's financial accounts.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable-quality systems show little material reduction in resource requirements during the target period.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Documented comparisons available for the target period show large reductions in resources per comparable-quality output, including materially greater output from the same hardware.

Its deployment tests report 5.76 times the generation throughput on an eight-H800 node using the earlier service's workload distribution, demonstrating substantial resource-efficiency gains.
